== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|western labyrinth{{!}}The labyrinth is an ancient, massive, and incredibly complex structure that spans the entire world. While it has many different names—including the [[Dreadgod labyrinth]], the First [[Tomb]], and the forgotten maze—its primary hub is located deep underground within [[Sacred Valley]]. The structure is characterized by its extreme difficulty to navigate because it constantly shifts and reconfigures its internal layout. Rather than a fixed physical map, understanding the labyrinth requires mastering the patterns that govern these constant changes. Functionally, the labyrinth serves as a sophisticated tool for spatial transportation; its various branches are conceptually treated as the same location regardless of their actual geographic position. It also possesses powerful defensive capabilities, including suppression fields that can weaken [[Dreadgods]] and security measures left behind by the ancient [[Soulsmiths]]. These defenses include legendary Script{{!}}script formations, invisible walls, and the ability to lock down spatial travel. western labyrinth{{!}}The labyrinth is also capable of preserving memories or echoes of individuals within its depths. The structure has had many different owners and guardians throughout history. It is currently controlled by [[Lindon]], who can command its movements and use its Authority{{!}}authority to manipulate space. western labyrinth{{!}}The labyrinth's origins are tied to ancient creators, including the seven founders and the [[Abidan]], and it contains various layers ranging from shallow outer rooms to deep, highly secured prisons and ancient workshops.}}

== Reaper ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|Serving as a repository for ancient truths and the workplace of legendary [[Soulsmiths]], the labyrinth is an environment that demands immense [[willpower]] to navigate. While its outer entrances can be opened by Underlord{{!}}Underlords, the facility is not locked and functions with a [[suppression field]] that was eventually deactivated. The interior consists of symbol-marked tunnels and chambers that shift seemingly at will through spatial transmission, even producing a roar that shakes the entire structure. Within its halls, which include a long oval room with a trench, the labyrinth has fed upon [[Mercy]]'s mother and was originally intended to serve as a prison for [[Subject One]]. During the exploration by [[Lindon]] and [[Yerin]], the labyrinth broke its own rules to trap them when its controller twisted space to lock the group in a room, eventually becoming the site of a battle between [[Lindon]] and [[Reigan Shen]].}}

== Dreadgod ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|Following his [[inheritance]] of the entire structure, Ozmanthus Arelius{{!}}Ozmanthus oversees a labyrinth that utilizes its branches for transportation. These tendrils spread beneath [[Sacred Valley]] and extend for a thousand miles, providing the majority of the energy required for travel through space. Within its shifting architecture, which features rooms that can be moved individually, the labyrinth contains various echoes and records. While a distant entrance remains visible, [[Lindon]], [[Dross]], and Ziel of the Wasteland{{!}}Ziel have already ventured inside.}}

== Waybound ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|western labyrinth{{!}}The labyrinth serves as a complex structure of scattered halls and reinforced [[stone]] walls that [[Lindon]] controls, having inherited it from his ancestors in [[Sacred Valley]] along with [[Eithan]] and the [[Abidan]]. It possesses functions that reach beyond boundaries, including the ability to fill gaps in projected memory patterns and preserve specific memories, such as those belonging to [[Northstrider]]. While the labyrinth's restoration Authority{{!}}authority is strained by the projection of the [[Wandering Titan]], whose appearance is depicted in its murals, it can also provide defensive [[scripts]] that allow [[Lindon]] to survive three [[Monarchs]] simultaneously. Beyond its physical presence, the labyrinth maintains a connection to everyone its [[hunger aura]] has ever fed on and can even move [[Lindon]] without a direct order.}}
